1.title: ConfigMaps and Secrets
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Config Maps and Secrets. It covers the exam area Application Environment, Configuration and Security. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Understand Config Maps. Create and consume Secrets. Practice with seven hands-on labs worth forty-three points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Application Environment, Configuration and Security (twenty-five percent). Practice in this module: seven labs, forty-three points, about forty-six minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: Keep configuration out of the image
1.text: Keep configuration out of the image. The figure shows this: Two ways to consume configuration. Exam tip: A Secret is base sixty-four encoded, not encrypted; a Pod only sees Config Maps and Secrets of its own namespace.

1.title: Keep configuration out of the image, continued
1.text: Keep configuration out of the image. An image should run unchanged in every environment. What differs (log level, U R Ls, passwords) lives in Config Maps (plain settings) and Secrets (sensitive values) and is handed to the Pod at start. Both are namespaced objects holding key or value pairs, and a Pod can only use those in its own namespace. For. Config Map: settings, config files. Secret: passwords, tokens, keys, certificates. Stored as. Config Map: plain text in data. Secret: base sixty-four in data (or plain in string Data when you write it). Size limit. Config Map: one mebibyte B. Secret: one mebibyte B. Types. Config Map: one. Secret: Opaque (default), Kubernetes dot io slash tls, Kubernetes dot io slash dockerconfigjson, Kubernetes dot io slash basic auth, Kubernetes dot io slash service account token,...

1.title: Keep configuration out of the image, continued
1.text: Keep configuration out of the image. base sixty-four is encoding, not encryption. Anyone who can read the Secret can decode it ( echo c GFzcw base sixty-four dash d ). A Secret is protected by R back, and optionally by encryption at rest in E T C D, not by base sixty-four.

1.title: Create them
1.text: Create them. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Create them, continued
1.text: Create them. Declarative Secret with plain text: use string Data and Kubernetes stores it encoded. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Create them, continued
1.text: Create them. Read a value back: kube control get secret db creds dash o json path dot data dot password base sixty-four dash d. A Config Map can also be immutable true (it can never change and must be replaced), which saves load on the A P I server.

1.title: Consume them: environment variables
1.text: Consume them: environment variables. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Environment variables are read once at start: after you change a Config Map, restart the Pods.

1.title: Consume them: environment variables, continued
1.text: Consume them: environment variables. Imperative shortcut on a running Deployment: kube control set env deployment app the from flag set to configmap slash settings (all keys) or kube control set env deployment app key value (a literal). A key that is not a valid variable name (it has a dash) is skipped by env From. Variables are read once, at container start. A changed Config Map or Secret does not change them in a running container: restart the Pods ( kube control rollout restart deployment app ).

1.title: Consume them: files
1.text: Consume them: files. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Mount one key as a single file in an existing directory with sub Path.

1.title: Consume them: files, continued
1.text: Consume them: files. mount the volume. the directory gets one file per key; the old content of that directory is hidden. items key x, path y. mount only some keys, with new file names. sub Path default dot conf on the volume Mount. mount one file into an existing directory without hiding the rest (such a file is not updated later). default Mode four hundred. file permissions (octal). optional true. the Pod starts even if the object or key is missing.

1.title: Consume them: files, continued
1.text: Consume them: files. Mounted files update by themselves, after a delay of up to a minute or two, when the Config Map or Secret changes (except sub Path mounts). The application must re-read the file. Mount a single key as one file in a directory that has other files. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Failure modes
1.text: Failure modes. create container config error. the Config Map, Secret or key named in value From does not exist (create it; the Pod then starts by itself). Pod stuck Container Creating, event Mount Volume dot Set Up failed... configmap x not found. a Config Map or Secret volume that does not exist (without optional ). Value looks right but the app still uses the old one. environment variables are not refreshed: restart the Pods. illegal base sixty-four data. a hand-encoded value with a trailing newline: encode with echo dash n. err image pull on a private image. missing or wrong image Pull Secrets. Exam tip. Use the imperative commands for the object and a short yamel for the Pod. To avoid indentation mistakes, generate the Pod with kube control run... the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml and add env or volumes to it.

1.title: Failure modes, continued
1.text: Failure modes. Exam tip. "Make the running Pods use the new value" means update the Config Map and restart the Deployment. Updating the Config Map alone is not enough for environment variables. Exam tip: create container config error means a referenced Config Map, Secret or key does not exist.

1.title: Lab 9.1: configmap env volume
1.text: Lab nine point one: configmap env volume. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace cfg, create a Config Map app config with the keys log level debug and color blue. Create a Pod cfgpod (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that. gets the environment variable log level from the Config Map key of the same name (not a hard-coded value), and. mounts the whole Config Map as files in the directory slash E T C slash app. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 9.1: configmap env volume, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n cfg create configmap app config the from literal flag set to log level debug the from literal flag set to color blue. kube control dash n cfg apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 9.1: configmap env volume, Solution, continued
1.text: Lab nine point one: configmap env volume, Solution, continued. Run volume Mounts. Then - name conf, mount Path slash E T C slash app. Then volumes. Then - name conf. Then config Map name app config. Then Y. Then kube control dash n cfg wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash cfgpod the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n cfg exec cfgpod then the command sh dash c echo log level cat slash E T C slash app slash color.

1.title: Lab 9.2: secret env file
1.text: Lab nine point two: secret env file. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace sec, create a Secret db creds with username admin and password S three cret exclamation mark. Create a Pod dbclient (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that gets the environment variable D B user from the Secret key username and mounts the whole Secret read-only at slash E T C slash db. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 9.2: secret env file, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n sec create secret generic db creds the from literal flag set to username admin the from literal flag set to password S three cret exclamation mark. kube control dash n sec apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 9.2: secret env file, Solution, continued
1.text: Lab nine point two: secret env file, Solution, continued. Run volume Mounts. Then - name creds, mount Path slash E T C slash db, read Only true. Then volumes. Then - name creds. Then secret secret Name db creds. Then Y. Then kube control dash n sec wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash dbclient the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n sec exec dbclient then the command sh dash c echo D B user cat slash E T C slash db slash password.

2.title: Lab 9.3: configmap from files
2.text: Lab nine point three: configmap from files. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The files about slash work slash app dot env (lines of key value ) and about slash work slash motd dot txt exist. In the namespace cfg, create a Config Map settings whose keys are the lines of app dot env (use the env-file option) and a second Config Map motd with one key motd that holds the content of motd dot txt. Then create a Pod envpod (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that loads all keys of settings as environment variables with env From and mounts the Config Map motd as files in slash E T C slash motd. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 9.3: configmap from files, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n cfg create configmap settings the from env file flag set to H O M E slash work slash app dot env. Then kube control dash n cfg create configmap motd the from file flag set to motd H O M E slash work slash motd dot txt. Then kube control dash n cfg get cm settings dash o yaml then pipe to head -twelve. kube control dash n cfg apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 9.3: configmap from files, Solution, continued
2.text: Lab nine point three: configmap from files, Solution, continued. Run volume Mounts. Then - name motd, mount Path slash E T C slash motd. Then volumes. Then - name motd. Then config Map name motd. Then Y. Then kube control dash n cfg wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash envpod the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n cfg exec envpod then the command sh dash c echo mode region cat slash E T C slash motd slash motd.

2.title: Lab 9.4: registry secret
2.text: Lab nine point four: registry secret. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace reg, create a Secret of the type docker registry named regcred for the registry registry dot example dot com with the username dev and the password pw one hundred twenty-three. Create a Pod private (image registry dot example dot com slash team slash app one dot zero ) that uses this Secret to pull its image ( image Pull Secrets ). The image does not exist, so the Pod is expected to stay in err image pull or image pull back off: only the configuration is checked. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 9.4: registry secret, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n reg create secret docker registry regcred the docker server flag set to registry dot example dot com the docker username flag set to dev the docker password flag set to, and so on. kube control dash n reg apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n reg get secret regcred dash o json path dot type echo. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 9.5: config change restart
2.text: Lab nine point five: config change restart. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace cfg, the Deployment cfgapp reads the key color of the Config Map site both as the environment variable color and as the file slash E T C slash site slash color. Change the value of color in the Config Map from blue to green, and make sure that the running Pods of the Deployment show green in the environment variable and in the file. Wait for the rollout to finish. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 9.5: config change restart, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n cfg patch configmap site dash p data color green. Then kube control dash n cfg rollout restart deployment cfgapp. Then kube control dash n cfg rollout status deployment cfgapp the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n cfg exec deploy slash cfgapp then the command sh dash c echo color cat slash E T C slash site slash color. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 9.6: secret decode
2.text: Lab nine point six: secret decode. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The Secret api key in the namespace sec stores an A P I token under the key token. Write the decoded token (just the plain text, no newline needed) to about slash answers slash token dot txt on the host where you run kube control. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 9.6: secret decode, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n sec get secret api key dash o json path dot data dot token base sixty-four dash d about slash answers slash token dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash token dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 9.7: configmap subpath file
2.text: Lab nine point seven: configmap subpath file. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace cfg, the Config Map proxy holds an engine X server configuration under the key default dot conf. Create a Pod gateway (image engine X alpine ) that mounts only that key as the single file slash E T C slash engine X slash conf dot d slash default dot conf (use sub Path, so that the other files of the directory stay). When the Pod is Ready, an H T T P request to it must return the text configured. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 9.7: configmap subpath file, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n cfg apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n cfg wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash gateway the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Are Secret values encrypted? Answer: No; they are base sixty-four encoded. Protect them with R back and encryption at rest. Question two. What is the difference between env with config Map Key Ref and env From? Answer: config Map Key Ref takes one chosen key; env From loads all keys as variables. Question three. Does an environment variable from a Config Map change when the Config Map changes? Answer: No; only after the Pod restarts. Mounted files do update.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How do you mount one key of a Config Map as a single file in an existing directory? Answer: Mount the volume with sub Path key and mount Path set to the full file path. Question five. Which command creates a Config Map whose keys come from the lines of a key value file? Answer: kube control create configmap name the from env file flag set to file. Question six. What does create container config error mean? Answer: A referenced Config Map, Secret or key does not exist.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. Which Secret type holds registry credentials, and which Pod field uses it? Answer: Kubernetes dot io slash dockerconfigjson (create it with docker registry ); the Pod's image Pull Secrets. Question eight. How do you read a Secret value on the command line? Answer: kube control get secret name dash o json path dot data. key base sixty-four dash d.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Create: the from literal flag, the from env file flag, the from file flag key path; create secret generic slash tls slash docker registry. Env: value From dot config Map Key Ref or secret Key Ref; env From for all keys. Files: volumes dot config Map or secret; items, sub Path, default Mode, read Only. Refresh: env: restart the Pods; files: updated by the kubelet (not sub Path ). Secret: base sixty-four, not encryption; string Data for plain input. Same namespace: a Pod only sees Config Maps and Secrets of its own namespace. Errors: create container config error, Mount Volume dot Set Up failed.
